carry_forward_verdicts.rationale: In crates/workspace-tests/tests/support/bin_path.rs, bin_path now runs the cargo build through crate::deadline::spawn_with_limit(&mut build, None, BIN_BUILD_DEADLINE). BIN_BUILD_DEADLINE is a separate named 20-minute constant, so the shared 60s SUBPROCESS_DEADLINE is unchanged. The runner in tests/support/deadline.rs bounds every wait. The try_wait loop is capped by the deadline. On expiry it kills the process group on Unix and panics with the captured stderr. Each stdout/stderr drain waits at most PIPE_GRACE (5s) through recv_timeout and never joins the reader thread. A cargo process stuck on a file lock, a network stall or a wedged rustc therefore fails the test instead of hanging. The assert message names the 'Blocking waiting for file lock' case and includes stderr. `--locked` is added. The retained BUILD_LOCK mutex only serialises threads in one process. A thread blocked on it waits at most one bounded build per queued caller, so no unbounded path remains. This is redesign, not masking: there is no retry, sleep or padded shared timeout. Every target that includes support (consumer_parity, git_read_parity, e2e_treesitter_producer, test_util_off) also declares `mod deadline;`, so the crate::deadline reference resolves in each. I could not run the tests, because I had read-only tools and no shell. The review rests on reading the code.

The bin_path verbatim target-dir cause is fixed in code. workspace_root() is built from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR and never canonicalized, so no \\?\ path reaches mimalloc's cl.exe build. The clippy large_enum_variant half is covered by the a6cd399 box commit. I did not inspect that commit or check CI myself. This verdict rests on the supplied evidence that PR 31 CI is 13/13 green at a7b68f6 (run 42433144889), including test (windows-2022).
